# `select_bands`

a band set as spans on the dataset's Frequency or Eigenvalue line, each band a quantity in a chart of the line.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run select_bands --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run select_bands --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run select_bands --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --rule frequency [--bands '["1-2 Hz","2-4 Hz","4-8 Hz"]']
nxr-neuro run select_bands --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --rule levels --surface cortex
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$surface"}, required false (rule levels: the surface whose grid's levels are the bands) | no |
| `grid` | selection ladder, manifold surface.manifold.0, where {"name": "{surface} tiles"}, required false (rule levels: the surface's tiles (`nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface` first)) | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rule` | `--rule` | `frequency` | - | frequency, eigenvalue, wavelength, parts, levels | frequency \| eigenvalue \| wavelength \| parts \| levels |
| `surface` | `--surface` | none | - |  | rules wavelength, parts, levels: the surface (its subject owns the spatial band set) |
| `bands` | `--bands` | none | Hz |  | the bands as quantities, each half open [lo, hi): Hz (chart linear or log10) for rule frequency, 1/m2 or mm for rule eigenvalue; optionally named {name, band}; required for the rules frequency, eigenvalue (no default band set), e.g. --bands '["8-12 Hz"]' |
| `scales` | `--scales` | none | mm |  | rules wavelength and parts: the named scales (hemisphere, lobe, region, gyrus) or quantities (wavelength 40 mm, parts 16) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{rule} bands` | - |  | the band set's name |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`select.bands`](../nodes.md) | grid=grid | rule=$rule, bands=$bands | bank |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Notes from the definition

```text
A BAND SET on a line: ONE maker (the node `select.bands`), spans on the dataset's FREQUENCY line (Hz; charts `linear` and `log10`) or on its EIGENVALUE line (1/m2; charts `eigenvalue` and `wavelength` in mm), every
band stated as a QUANTITY in a chart of that line, never an index. A single band SELECTS (it is no frequency axis); several bands are one band SET whose members include the bands. A consumer takes the set
through its `bands` edge, never re-making it from parameters.

  rule frequency   a list of bands in Hz (or log10 Hz), named; no default band set: `--bands` is required
  rule eigenvalue  spans in the eigenvalue chart (1/m2) or the wavelength chart (mm)
  rule wavelength  named scales by wavelength (the named scales of `scales.h`: hemisphere, lobe, region, gyrus)
  rule parts       named scales by parts per hemisphere
  rule levels      a dyadic grid's levels, each level's Weyl band (needs the grid; was `spatial_bands`)

The band's span is half open [lo, hi); the code is the band's position in the list, the lookup carries {name, lo, hi, unit, chart}. A transform's bins are NOT a line made here: the Frequency line is the dataset's own
(nxr `convert.frequency`, 0.5 Hz steps to 500 Hz), and a transform's output carries its made line as a factor.

  nxr-neuro run select_bands --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --rule frequency [--bands '["1-2 Hz","2-4 Hz","4-8 Hz"]']
  nxr-neuro run select_bands --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --rule levels --surface cortex
```
